title: Receiving apostles, rejecting forgeries, and the mixed gospel of Peter
english: For we, brothers and sisters, receive Peter and the other apostles as we receive Christ, but as people with experience we reject the forgeries written in their name, knowing that we did not receive such things. When I was with you, I was supposing that all of you were conducting yourselves in right faith, and without examining the gospel they were putting forward under Peter's name, I said, "If this is the only thing that seems to cause you smallness of soul, let it be read." But now, having learned from what was told to me that their mind was harboring some heresy, I will make haste to come to you again. So, brothers and sisters, expect me soon.

But we, brothers and sisters, having grasped what kind of heresy Marcion belonged to—he who was even contradicting himself, not understanding what he was saying, as you will learn from what has been written to you—we were able, from others who had studied this very gospel, that is, from the successors of those who originated it, whom we call Docetists (for most of their thoughts come from that teaching), to borrow it from them and go through it, and to find that most of it agrees with the true teaching of the Savior, but some things have been added, which we have also listed for you.

orientation: Serapion, bishop of Antioch, opens his letter to the church at Rhossus by stating the principle that he and the church receive the apostles as Christ but reject writings falsely attributed to them, then recounts his earlier permission and his later discovery of heresy and of additions in the gospel attributed to Peter.
